issue: Per-version e2e evidence is one file per (module, layer, version). The spec does not say where per-browser cell evidence lives, or how a Firefox-only tier-2 run for version V merges with V's existing tier-1 Chromium evidence.
implementation_impact: A tier-2 Firefox run overwrites <module>-e2e-<ver>.json and erases V's Chromium evidence. The release gate then reruns Chromium or loses it.
suggestion: Specify per-cell storage: either <module>-e2e-<ver>-<browser>.json or a read-merge of a browsers{engine: {...}} map inside the per-version file, with per-engine provenance.

issue: Freshness is judged by file mtime against source mtime. Once several browser cells share one file, a later write for one engine refreshes the mtime of older content for another engine.
implementation_impact: Chromium evidence recorded before a patch looks fresh after a post-patch Firefox write, so ready can be true on stale evidence.
suggestion: Store a per-cell run timestamp and source-mtime snapshot (or source hash), and judge freshness per cell, not per file.

issue: 'Clean' is not defined for tier promotion. Nothing says whether an inconclusive cell (boot timeout, skipped_image, install failure, skipped_browser, launch error) counts as clean.
implementation_impact: Either the next tier starts on an untested canary, or tiering stalls forever on an infra failure with no stated recovery.
suggestion: Define clean = conclusive pass with full scenarios. State that inconclusive halts promotion, report the infra cause, and offer retry or a narrowed run.

issue: The canary browser is configurable, but tier 1 covers only 'other versions × Chromium'. If the canary browser is Firefox, the canary-version × Chromium cell belongs to no tier.
implementation_impact: That cell never runs, so ready stays false permanently. Or the planner invents an unspecified extra run.
suggestion: Define tier 1 as (all versions × all browsers in tier-1 engine set) minus the canary cell, or forbid a non-Chromium canary browser.

issue: The canary is configurable, but nothing says what happens when the configured canary version or browser is outside psm_target_versions / psm_e2e_browsers or outside the operator-narrowed --versions/--browsers.
implementation_impact: Tier 0 tests a cell that is not in the target set, or crashes, and promotion rests on irrelevant evidence.
suggestion: Validate the canary against the effective target set. On a mismatch, fall back to newest target × first browser, or exit 2 with a clear message.

issue: Empty tiers are not handled. Examples: one target version (tier 1 empty), or browsers narrowed to Chromium only (tier 2 Firefox empty or absent).
implementation_impact: Promotion logic may wait forever on an empty tier, or treat a narrowed set as release-gate complete.
suggestion: Treat an empty tier as vacuously clean for promotion only. Keep ready=false whenever a configured mandatory browser or version was excluded.

issue: When a cell fails in tier 2 for a Firefox-specific reason, the loop returns to tier 0, whose cell is canary-version × Chromium. That cell cannot reproduce the failure. (This is the browser dimension, which the version open question does not cover.)
implementation_impact: The canary passes immediately and promotes without the fix being exercised. The loop runs a full cold fan-out each time.
suggestion: On a tier-1/2 failure, the fix-loop cell = the failing (version, browser) until it passes, then resume the canary progression.

issue: Fail-fast triggers on a 'conclusive blocking finding'. It does not say whether an inconclusive infra failure in the first cell also stops new cells. With --jobs concurrency, 'first' is also undefined.
implementation_impact: After a boot failure the run either burns the full matrix on a broken daemon or stops inconsistently. Results are nondeterministic across runs.
suggestion: State that infra-inconclusive does not trigger fail-fast (or does, explicitly). Define 'first' as the first finding reported in completion order.

issue: The persistence of not-run cells is unspecified. Nothing says whether a not-run cell writes a per-version file that overwrites a previous evidence file for that cell, or writes nothing.
implementation_impact: Prior gate-grade evidence for an unrelated cell can be clobbered. Or a not-run cell leaves an old file that the planner reuses as fresh.
suggestion: Not-run cells write no evidence file and appear only in the run report and aggregate as not-run. The planner keeps judging the existing file by freshness.

issue: Failed-only rerun has no defined behavior when the latest evidence is missing, inconclusive with no failed scenarios, or itself partial, or when failed scenarios were renamed or deleted since.
implementation_impact: Chained partial reruns shrink the scenario set and hide regressions in previously passing scenarios. A rerun with an empty set may report clean.
suggestion: Derive the failed set only from the latest full-scenario evidence for that cell. If none exists or the set is empty, run full. Drop unknown scenario names with a note.

issue: A failed-only rerun skips scenarios that may set up state for later ones (ordering dependence, BO login via ctx bo_authed, config set by an earlier spec).
implementation_impact: The rerun reports false failures, or false passes from missing preconditions, which misdirects the fix loop.
suggestion: Require specs to declare dependencies, or run failed scenarios plus their declared prerequisites, marking prerequisite results as non-evidence.

issue: It is unspecified which browser a failed-only rerun uses when the latest evidence for the version has failures in a different engine than the canary browser.
implementation_impact: The rerun drives the wrong engine and reports pass while the actual failing cell stays unexercised.
suggestion: Key the failed set per (version, browser) and rerun on the same engine that failed.

issue: The warm container outlives the invocation that booted it. --cleanup-orphans removes artifacts whose owner PID is dead, so between iterations the owner is dead by design.
implementation_impact: Another session's --cleanup-orphans deletes the warm canary mid-loop, and the next iteration fails or cold-boots silently.
suggestion: Give the warm container a lease (label psm.keepalive-until or a persistent owner process). Have --cleanup-orphans skip unexpired leases and reap expired ones.

issue: Each ps-run-layer invocation creates a new Job ID, but the warm container keeps the Job ID of the invocation that booted it. The spec does not say which ID later iterations log under, or which ID --stop-job targets.
implementation_impact: The operator stops the wrong job, or cannot stop the warm container by the ID shown in the current run.
suggestion: Keep a stable warm-container Job ID that is reused and printed by every iteration (e.g. --reuse-job <id>). Log both run ID and container job ID.

issue: There is no health check or fallback for a warm container that died, became unhealthy, lost its DB, or runs a different image tag than the current tag map or config resolves.
implementation_impact: The iteration fails as infra or tests the wrong PrestaShop image, and the evidence is attributed to the wrong provenance.
suggestion: Before each warm iteration, verify the container is running and healthy and that its image tag equals resolve_tag. Otherwise tear it down and cold boot, logging the reason.

issue: The DB reset to the post-boot baseline does not say when the baseline is captured, how it is restored, or what happens if capture or restore fails. Patched source sync into the container and PHP or Symfony cache invalidation are also unspecified.
implementation_impact: Stale opcache or cache, or a failed reset, lets the previous iteration's code or data produce findings, which CAP-5 explicitly forbids.
suggestion: Snapshot the DB right after wait-healthy and before install. Restore it, clear the PS cache, and reset opcache each iteration. A failed restore marks the iteration inconclusive and forces a cold boot.

issue: The end of the warm-container lifecycle is unspecified: who tears it down at promotion (tier 0's last run must be cold), when the canary cell changes, when the loop is abandoned, or on session exit.
implementation_impact: Idle warm containers accumulate on the shared WSL daemon, holding RAM and ports and causing wait-healthy stalls for tier 1.
suggestion: Tear down the warm container before the cold promotion run and on canary change. Set an idle TTL after which the lease expires and --cleanup-orphans reaps it.

issue: The single concurrency cap has no accounting rule. It does not say whether a slot is a container or a browser, whether an idle warm container counts, or what CAP-7 does when the cap leaves no room for two browsers (e.g. cap=1).
implementation_impact: The cap is either exceeded, saturating the daemon, or CAP-7 deadlocks waiting for a slot.
suggestion: Define cost per container and per browser, and count the warm container. When the remaining cap is below 2, run the version's browsers sequentially and log the fallback.

issue: Running browsers in parallel shares per-version state: the ctx dict (bo_authed), the per-version screenshot dir and file names, and console and screenshot rollups. The browser phase has no timeout (phase timeout None), so one hung engine blocks the version indefinitely.
implementation_impact: Engines clobber each other's screenshots or auth state, so findings differ from a sequential run. A hung engine stalls the whole tier.
suggestion: Give each engine its own ctx copy and a screenshot subdir per engine. Add a per-engine phase timeout that marks only that cell inconclusive.

issue: Timing semantics are unspecified for phases that do not occur (warm run: no bring-up or wait-healthy), for phases that timed out or failed, for unlisted phases (pull, wait-http, warmup-bo, teardown), and for overlapping parallel browsers.
implementation_impact: The aggregate mixes null and 0, double-counts overlapped time, or omits pull, so the boot-vs-browser comparison is misleading.
suggestion: Record {phase: {seconds, outcome}} for every phase. Absent phases are omitted (not 0). Report the per-version wall-clock separately from the per-engine sums.

issue: The progress log is truncated at each run, and per-version files are rewritten per tier. The spec does not say which run's timings the aggregate surfaces when a cell's evidence came from tiers or runs other than the latest.
implementation_impact: The aggregate shows timings from the wrong run, or only the last run, so tier 0 versus gate costs are not visible.
suggestion: Store timings inside each cell's evidence record with the run ID and tier. The aggregate lists timings per cell from the evidence actually used.

issue: Tiering and fail-fast introduce not-run and partial cell states, but the spec does not map them onto the existing headless per-version verdict contract.
implementation_impact: psm-develop and others misread not-run as pass or fail, or break on an unknown field value.
suggestion: Define the mapping explicitly: not-run or partial → per-version verdict 'inconclusive' with a reason. Extend headless.md accordingly.

issue: Promotion between tiers has no defined trigger: automatic, operator-confirmed in interactive mode, or caller-driven in headless mode. Headless runs also cannot pull images, so a missing canary image blocks tier 0.
implementation_impact: Interactive runs launch hours-long cold tiers without consent, or headless runs stall at tier 0 with no verdict.
suggestion: State that interactive mode asks before tier 1/2 while headless mode auto-promotes. A missing canary image in headless mode returns blocked with the reason.

issue: Freshness compares evidence mtime with source mtime. Nothing handles a source patch that lands while a cell is running (now more likely during the warm fix loop).
implementation_impact: Evidence from the pre-patch code gets an mtime later than the patch and is reused as fresh at the gate.
suggestion: Record the source mtime or hash at run start in the evidence. The planner compares that recorded value against the current source.
